[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

'''James Glasgow''' was born about 1748, the son of '''[[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]]''' and his wife '''[[Unknown-763010|Ann Glasgow]]'''. His approximate year of birth is calculated from his age at death.<ref name="Armorial">"Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim," ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', second series 6 (1900), [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up p. 47], Glasgow monument inscription.</ref>

The family monument explicitly identifies James as the son of Hugh and Ann Glasgow. Hugh died on 8 July 1767, aged 62, and Ann died on 8 June 1786, aged 75.<ref name="Armorial" />

James married '''[[Unknown-763421|Jane]]''', whose maiden name is not given in the monument inscription. Jane was born about 1741, based on her recorded age at death.<ref name="Armorial" />

James and Jane had at least one known child:

* '''[[Glasgow-3992|Ann Glasgow]]''', born about 1768; died 25 May 1832, aged 64.<ref name="Armorial" />

James died on '''14 April 1812''', aged 64.<ref name="Armorial" /> His stated age places his birth approximately between 15 April 1747 and 14 April 1748.

His wife Jane survived him. She died on '''21 July 1820''', aged 79.<ref name="Armorial" />

=== Tanner at Larne ===

James is probably the Larne tanner documented between 1768 and 1790. A 1768 assignment by a different James Glasgow, a ropemaker, was witnessed by James Glasgow, tanner. The tanner later swore to the deed's execution at Larne.<ref name="Tanner1768">Registry of Deeds transcript, assignment dated 28 March 1768, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDXW FamilySearch image].</ref>

A mortgage dated 22 June 1778 concerning premises in Newtown of Larne was witnessed by James Glasgow of Larne, tanner, and John Weir, notary. James swore the supporting affidavit at Larne on 29 June 1778.<ref name="Tanner1778">Registry of Deeds transcript, mortgage dated 22 June 1778, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-64YW FamilySearch image].</ref>

The occupation, place and chronology also agree with the 1786 Blackcave lease to James Glasgow, tanner of Larne. The sequence is a strong identity match, although the deeds do not name his wife or relatives. He should not be confused with the older Larne ropemaker [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]].

A lease dated 14 January 1784 was witnessed by James Glasgow of Larne, '''tanner''', with Samuel Drummond, merchant, and James Farries, writing clerk. James’s affidavit was sworn 17 August 1790; the memorial was registered on 23 August. The original reads “Tanner”, resolving an earlier automated “Turner” reading. This strengthens the occupational sequence, without independently naming his family.<ref name="Tanner1784">Registry of Deeds, memorial 278037, lease 14 January 1784, sworn 17 August and registered 23 August 1790, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ4-4SJF FamilySearch image 437], original inspected 21 September 2026. The online collection label 1734–1736 does not describe this image’s date.</ref>

=== Family Monument ===

The Glasgow armorial monument records Hugh Glasgow and Ann Glasgow, followed by:

:''James Glasgow their Son who died the 14th of April 1812 aged 64 years. Also his wife Jane Glasgow died 21st July 1820 aged 79 years. And of Ann Glasgow, Daughter to the last named who died the 25th May 1832 aged 64 years.''<ref name="Armorial" />

The same monument also commemorates eleven children of Hugh and Ann, naming a daughter Jane as "the first" and a son Hugh as "the last". James is recorded separately and explicitly described as "their Son".<ref name="Armorial" />

=== Research Notes ===

James's exact date and place of birth have not yet been established. His birth year of about 1748 is derived from his stated age of 64 at his death on 14 April 1812.

The wording concerning the eleven children of Hugh and Ann should not be interpreted as proving that the younger Hugh was their youngest child. The monument appears to refer to a particular group of children buried or commemorated there, while James is subsequently identified separately as their son.

Jane's maiden surname is currently unknown. The inscription calls her "his wife Jane Glasgow", which records her married surname rather than establishing Glasgow as her birth surname.

=== Newtown title succession: identities unresolved ===

An 1874 deed recites a lease to James Glasgow dated 2 October 1779 and its renewal to Anne Glasgow and Jane Glasgow on 25 February 1832. The north-side Newtown property, formerly John English’s, adjoined a tenement formerly Hugh Glasgow’s. This documents succession to a lease, but does not call the women James’s daughters or identify which James held it. The monument wife Jane died in 1820 and cannot automatically be the 1832 Jane. [[Glasgow-3992|Ann Glasgow]], whose monument gives a May 1832 death, is only a candidate for Anne; the original renewal is needed.<ref name="Newtown1874">Registry of Deeds, Antrim to John Mulvenna, indenture 25 March 1874, registered 24 August 1874, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77Q4-H FamilySearch image 475], recital inspected in the original; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77QC-T continuation image 476].</ref>

=== Uncertain son: the 1843 settlement testator ===

[[Glasgow-4180|Hugh Glasgow]], whose executors or trustees were to pay £250 in the 1843 marriage settlement of [[Glasgow-4181|Mary Glasgow]] and John McGavock, is attached here as an '''uncertain son'''. Neither this father-son relationship nor Hugh's proposed fatherhood of Mary is stated in the settlement.<ref>Registry of Deeds, Ireland, marriage settlement, John McGavock and Mary Glasgow, 10 February 1843, affidavit 14 February and registration 18 February; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-FQ3Q opening image 499] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-F3BZ continuation image 500], original images inspected 21 September 2026.</ref> James's documented generation and father Hugh make this a compatible working placement, not proof. Hugh's estimated birth about 1770 was chosen for this model and cannot independently support it. [[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-3931|Hugh Glasgow]] remain alternative fathers. Jane has not been assigned as the testator's mother. Hugh's will and Mary's earlier property title are needed to test the proposed chain.
